---
title: "Codebook (v0.1, draft)"
---

## Case definition

A passage counts as a **conspiratorial claim** if it asserts that identifiable actors are secretly coordinating an action for a hidden purpose. Excluded: allegations of incompetence without coordination; ordinary rumor without a covert actor; policy criticism.

## Unit

The **claim variant**: (alleged conspirators, covert action, target, stated purpose, evidence offered). A change in conspirators, action, or purpose creates a new variant with a recorded parent.

## Fields coded per occurrence

| Field | Values | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Tier | fringe / intermediary / elite | Source role, fixed before coding |
| Timestamp | ISO datetime; recording vs. upload noted | Retain uncertainty |
| Speaker identity | account / host / guest / writer / pseudonym | For the personnel route |
| Stance | endorse / raise as concern / neutral quote / reject | Adoption = endorse or raise-as-concern only |
| Asserted provenance | named fringe source / "people are saying" / anonymous reports / constituents / expert / other elite / none | Transformation C |
| Wording register | explicit / coded / euphemistic; stigmatized terms present (0/1) | Transformation A |
| Messenger | same actor as prior occurrence / new actor | Transformation B |
| Constituency frame | present / absent | Responsiveness justification |
| Evidence of transmission | explicit citation / link or screenshot / distinctive borrowed detail / chronology only | Sequence is not borrowing |
| Exact span | quoted text or audio time | Required for every coded field |

## Reliability plan

Two coders on a 300-passage subsample; report Krippendorff's alpha for stance and same-allegation judgments; freeze rules before the held-out evaluation set.
